extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for international patent protection under the PCT, patent attorneys/agents, and national/designated/elected patent offices
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, timelines, and rights relating to international applications filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), including publication, transmittal, preliminary examination, amendments, confidentiality, and national/elected/designated Office interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, the international publication of the international application shall be effected promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the priority date. The applicant may request earlier publication; the International Bureau shall proceed accordingly as provided in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of the international search report or declaration is governed by the Regulations. There shall be no international publication if the application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn before technical preparations for publication are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of immoral or disparaging content from publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau considers expressions or drawings contrary to morality or public order, or disparaging statements (as defined in the Regulations), it may omit such passages from its publications, indicating place and number of words/drawings omitted and furnishing, upon request, individual copies of the passages omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omissions must be indicated in the publication; applicants may request copies of omitted passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy, translation and fee to designated Offices (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a copy of the international application and a translation thereof (as prescribed), and pay the national fee (if any), to each designated Office not later than at the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Where national law allows later provision of inventor data, those indications must be furnished to the national Office not later than 30 months from the priority date unless contained in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the International Searching Authority declares no ISR will be established, the time limit for furnishing copies/translations/fees is the same. Any national law may fix later time limits for performing these acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on national processing prior to Article 22 time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall process or examine the international application prior to the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding this restriction, a designated Office may, on the express request of the applicant, process or examine the international application at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of international effect in designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the international application in any designated State shall cease (with consequences of withdrawal of a national application) if the applicant withdraws the international application or the designation, if the application is considered withdrawn under specified Articles, or if the applicant fails to perform the acts referred to in Article 22 within the applicable time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding this, any designated Office may maintain the effect provided for in Article 11(3) even where it is not required by Article 25(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by designated Offices of refusals/declarations/findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a receiving Office has refused to accord an international filing date or declared the application withdrawn, or where the International Bureau has made a finding under Article 12(3), the International Bureau shall, at the request of the applicant, promptly send copies of any document in the file to designated Offices named by the applicant. Designated Offices shall decide whether the refusal, declaration or finding was justified under the Treaty and Regulations and, if due to error/omission by the receiving Office or International Bureau, treat the application as if such error had not occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be presented within the prescribed time limit. If the record copy reached the IB late due to applicant error/omission, the relief in subparagraph (a) applies only under Article 48(2) circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to correct before designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall reject an international application on the grounds of non-compliance with Treaty/Regulations without first giving the applicant the opportunity to correct the application to the extent and according to the procedure provided by the national law for the same or comparable situations for national applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction procedures follow national law provisions for comparable national application situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on national form/content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No national law shall require compliance with requirements relating to the form or contents of the international application different from or additional to those provided for in the Treaty and the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation does not affect Article 7(2) nor preclude national laws from requiring certain items once processing in the designated Office has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require additional documents once processing started
rubrics_metrics.description: Once processing of the international application has started in the designated Office, national law may require furnishing, for example, (i) when applicant is a legal entity, the name of an officer entitled to represent it, and (ii) documents not part of the international application but constituting proof of allegations or statements made in that application, including confirmation by signature where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements apply only after processing has started in the designated Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file under national law
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant, for purposes of any designated State, is not qualified according to the national law of that State to file a national application because he is not the inventor, the international application may be rejected by the designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation does not override national eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of more favorable national requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where national law provides requirements for national applications that are more favorable to applicants than the Treaty/Regulations, that national Office (and courts/competent organs) may apply the former requirements to international applications, except where the applicant insists that Treaty/Regulations requirements be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can elect to have Treaty/Regulations requirements applied instead of more favorable national ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to prescribe substantive patentability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Treaty and Regulations is intended to limit the freedom of each Contracting State to prescribe such substantive conditions of patentability as it desires. Definitions of prior art in the Treaty/Regulations are exclusively for international procedure purposes; Contracting States remain free to apply their national criteria for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National substantive patentability and prior art rules prevail at national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require evidence of substantive patentability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law may require that the applicant furnish evidence in respect of any substantive condition of patentability prescribed by such law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated/elected Offices may request evidentiary proof per national substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and address requirements under national law
rubrics_metrics.description: Any receiving Office or, once processing has started in the designated Office, that Office may apply national law as far as it relates to requirements that the applicant be represented by an agent having rights before that Office and/or that the applicant have an address in the designated State for receiving notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural representation/address rules are governed by national law where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security and economic restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Treaty and Regulations limits the freedom of any Contracting State to apply measures deemed necessary for preservation of national security or to limit, for protection of general economic interests, the right of its residents or nationals to file international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may impose national restrictions for security or economic reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment rights before designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall be given the opportunity to amend the claims, the description, and the drawings before each designated Office within the prescribed time limit. No designated Office shall grant or refuse a patent before such time limit has expired except with the express consent of the applicant. Amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed unless national law permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be in accordance with national law where the Treaty/Regulations are silent; where translation is required, amendments must be in translation language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effects of international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as protection of any rights of the applicant in a designated State is concerned, the effects in that State of the international publication shall, subject to paragraphs (2)–(4), be the same as those which the national law provides for compulsory national publication of unexamined national applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication language differs from national publication language, national law may require a translation to be published/made available/transmitted to an unauthorized user before effects apply. Applicant may request effects to be applicable only from 18 months from priority date. National law may provide effects apply only from date a copy is received by the national Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international application pre-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau and International Searching Authorities shall not allow access to the international application before international publication unless requested or authorized by the applicant. No national Office shall allow third-party access before the earliest of (i) date of international publication, (ii) receipt of communication under Article 20, or (iii) receipt of a copy under Article 22, unless requested/authorized by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for transmittals to ISAs, Article 13 transmittals, Article 20 communications, judicial purposes, and limited publication that identifies only receiving Office, applicant name, international filing date/number, and title of invention. 'Access' covers any means third parties may acquire cognizance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and form of the demand for international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any eligible applicant (residents/nationals as defined) may make a demand for international preliminary examination. The demand must be made separately from the international application, contain prescribed particulars, and be in the prescribed language and form. It shall indicate elected States and be subject to payment of prescribed fees within prescribed time limits and submission to the competent International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly may allow persons from States not party to the Treaty to make a demand if declared permissible. Additional elections may be made later; notifications follow prescribed channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and competence of the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination shall be carried out by the IPEA. For certain demands, the receiving Office or the Assembly shall, in accordance with applicable agreements, specify the competent IPEA(s). Provisions applicable to ISAs (Article 16(3)) apply mutatis mutandis to IPEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence and agreements between IPEAs and the International Bureau determine which authority handles the demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective and substantive criteria of international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the international preliminary examination is to formulate a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (to be non‑obvious), and to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT purposes: novelty = not anticipated by prior art as defined in the Regulations; inventive step = not obvious to a person skilled in the art at the prescribed relevant date; industrial applicability = can be made or used in any kind of industry (broadest sense). The IPEA shall consider all documents cited in the international search report and may consider additional relevant documents. Any Contracting State may apply additional or different criteria at national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure before the IPEA: communication, amendments, and opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure is governed by the Treaty, Regulations, and agreement between the IB and the IPEA. Applicant has a right to communicate orally and in writing with the IPEA, and to amend claims/description/drawings in the prescribed manner and within prescribed time limits before the IPER is established. Amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant shall receive at least one written opinion unless the IPEA considers that (i) the invention satisfies Article 33(1) criteria, (ii) the application complies with requirements checked by the Authority, and (iii) no observations are intended under Article 35(2) last sentence. Applicant may respond to written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention handling during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA considers the application lacks unity, it may invite the applicant to restrict the claims to comply or to pay additional fees. If the applicant does not comply within the prescribed time limit, the IPEA shall establish an IPER on those parts relating to what appears to be the main invention and indicate relevant facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law of any elected State may treat parts not examined as withdrawn unless a special fee is paid to the national Office. Restrictions chosen by the applicant may have national-law effects including being considered withdrawn in some States unless fees are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to carry out international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA considers that the application relates to subject matter on which it is not required to carry out an international preliminary examination, or that the description/claims/drawings are so unclear or claims inadequately supported that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability, the IPEA shall not go into those questions and shall inform the applicant of this opinion and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such situation applies only to certain claims, the IPEA's action applies only to those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and limitations of the international preliminary examination report (IPER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPER shall be established within the prescribed time limit and form. It shall not contain any statement on whether the claimed invention is patentable under any national law. It shall state, in relation to each claim, whether the claim appears to satisfy the criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability as defined for international preliminary examination, accompanied by citation of documents believed to support the conclusion and explanations as circumstances require. It shall also include other observations as Regulations provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IPEA finds situations under Article 34(4)(a), the report shall state that opinion and reasons and shall not contain the statements required by paragraph (2). If Article 34(4)(b) situation exists for certain claims, the report will treat those claims accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal, translation and communication of the IPER and annexes
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPER, together with prescribed annexes, shall be transmitted to the applicant and the International Bureau. The IPER and annexes shall be translated into prescribed languages. Any translation of the report is prepared by or under responsibility of the International Bureau; translations of annexes by the applicant. The IPER, its translation and annexes (in original language) shall be communicated by the IB to each elected Office; translations of annexes must be transmitted by the applicant within the prescribed time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 20(3) provisions apply mutatis mutandis to copies of any document cited in the IPER and not cited in the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of demand or election and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw any or all elections. If all elected States are withdrawn the demand is considered withdrawn. Withdrawals must be notified to the International Bureau which notifies elected Offices and the IPEA. Subject to subparagraph (b), withdrawal of the demand or election shall, unless national law provides otherwise, be considered withdrawal of the international application as far as that State is concerned; withdrawal prior to expiration of the applicable Article 22 time limit is not considered withdrawal of the international application (subject to national laws concerning receipt of copies/translations/fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National laws may provide different effects; timing relative to Article 22 time limits is determinative for effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the international preliminary examination file
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the International Bureau nor the IPEA shall, unless requested or authorized by the applicant, allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination by any person or authority at any time, except by elected Offices once the IPER has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Articles 36(1) and (3) and 37(3)(b), neither the IB nor the IPEA shall give information on issuance or non‑issuance of an IPER, or on withdrawal/nonwithdrawal of the demand or any election, unless requested/authorized by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy, translation and fee obligations to elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: If the election of any Contracting State has been effected prior to the expiration of the 19th month from the priority date, the applicant shall furnish a copy of the international application and a translation thereof (as prescribed), and pay the national fee (if any), to each elected Office not later than at the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. National law may fix later time limits for performing these acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perform these acts within the time limit causes cessation of the Article 11(3) effect in the elected State (with national withdrawal consequences), although elected Offices may maintain effect regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying of national examination for elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: If election of a Contracting State has been effected prior to the expiration of the 19th month, the national Office of that State shall not proceed to examination and other processing prior to the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 39, subject to paragraph (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding the delay, any elected Office may, on express request of the applicant, proceed to examination and other processing at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment rights before elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall be given the opportunity to amend the claims, description, and drawings, before each elected Office within the prescribed time limit. No elected Office shall grant or refuse a patent before such time limit has expired except with the express consent of the applicant. Amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed unless national law permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must comply with the national law of the elected State in all respects not provided for in the Treaty/Regulations; where translation is required, amendments shall be in the translation language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on requiring examination papers from other elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: No elected Office receiving the international preliminary examination report may require that the applicant furnish copies, or information on the contents, of any papers connected with the examination relating to the same international application in any other elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents forced sharing of national examination files between elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking different kinds of protection in designated/elected States
rubrics_metrics.description: In respect of any designated or elected State whose law provides for grants of inventors' certificates, utility certificates, utility models, patents or certificates of addition, the applicant may indicate (as prescribed) that the international application is for grant of such other kinds of protection rather than a patent, or vice versa, and the ensuing effect shall be governed by the applicant's choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this Article and Rules thereunder, Article 2(ii) shall not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking two kinds of protection simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Where national law permits an application to be for grant of a patent or other kinds of protection while also being for grant of another of those kinds, the applicant may indicate (as prescribed) the two kinds of protection sought; the effect shall be governed by the applicant's indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 2(ii) does not apply for the purposes of this Article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with regional patent treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional patent treaties may provide that international applications designating or electing a State party to both the regional patent treaty and the PCT may be filed as applications for such regional patents. National law of such States may provide that any designation or election in the international application shall have the effect of indicating the wish to obtain a regional patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional treaties and national law determine the procedural interaction and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for incorrect translations affecting patent scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If, because of an incorrect translation of the international application, the scope of any patent granted on that application exceeds the scope of the international application in its original language, the competent authorities of the Contracting State may retroactively limit the scope of the patent and declare it null and void to the extent that its scope exceeded the original-language scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation accuracy is crucial; authorities have power to limit or annul over‑broad patents caused by translation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation and modification of time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Details for computing time limits referred to in the Treaty are governed by the Regulations. All time limits fixed in Chapters I and II may, outside any revision under Article 60, be modified by decision of the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications must be made unanimously in the Assembly or by correspondence; procedural details are governed by the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for delays in meeting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any time limit fixed in the Treaty or Regulations is not met because of interruption in the mail service or unavoidable loss or delay in the mail, the time limit shall be deemed met in the cases and subject to the proof and other conditions prescribed in the Regulations. Any Contracting State shall, as far as that State is concerned, excuse delays for reasons admitted under its national law; a Contracting State may also excuse delays for other reasons as it sees fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is subject to the proof and conditions in the Regulations and to national law discretion.
